summary: Post-incident remediation kickoff after long-tail KV cache evictions that caused latency spikes for Tidewell. Goal: agree playbook, owners, short-term fixes and long-term reliability work to prevent recurrence.
topics: Root cause hypothesis (KV cache eviction + autoscaler interaction)
Rollout plan and rollback safety nets
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-27
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood CSM) — Priya, Carlos, Leanne, Samir (Tidewell)

Summary: quick kickoff to align on RCA, immediate mitigations and the remediation sprint cadence. Some audio glitches in the first 3 minutes.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i know it's the week between holidays so appreciate the time. we'll run quick through the timeline, what we think happened, and then owners for the repair playbook.
[00:18] Priya: thanks, Jordan. quick heads up — i'm on mobile so audio maybe choppy.
[00:25] Jordan: got it. carlos, can you summarize impact in 30s?
[00:30] Carlos: yeah — from our side, between 10:40 and 11:15 last thurs we saw 30–45% p95 latency spikes on the document enrichment path, we had ~8% error rate on generation calls, some timeouts bubbled to the app tier. it correlates with heavy batch sweeps and eviction spikes in the KV cache.
[00:52] Sofia: just to clarify, when you say "KV cache evictions" — do you mean local worker cache or global redis-style?
[00:58] Carlos: it's the in-memory KV per-gpu shard — it's our LRU trimming that kicked off under memory pressure. sometimes the runtime re-segments and we see cold KV misses which force regen of cached KV for long contexts.
[01:20] Leanne: business impact was a few customer-facing delays — tickets opened, some churn risk, that's why we asked for an RCA and playbook.
[01:30] Jordan: understood. quick note — logs we pulled show autoscaler upsizing and then a cascade where warmup didn't complete before traffic routed. so hypothesis: autoscale + KV garbage + routing timing.
[01:45] Priya: there were config changes night before — we bumped pool target to handle holiday load. could be related.
[01:52] Sofia: ok. so high level root cause hypothesis: (1) config bump increased device churn, (2) eviction policy on per-shard KV caused cache thrash, (3) request routing sent traffic to nodes not fully warmed. any disagreement?
[02:10] Carlos: sounds right. also saw heavier short TTLs on cached prefixes causing more regen. might be a prefetch/prefetching mis-tune — we left it aggressive.
[02:28] Jordan: good — that's the working hypothesis. immediate mitigations we discussed in the slack thread were: 1) temporarily cap autoscale to current pool size to stop churn, 2) raise memory buffer for KV cache, 3) change routing to prefer warmed nodes where possible. which ones are viable short-term?
[02:50] Priya: we can cap autoscale immediately. not a permanent fix but yes to start.
[02:55] Samir: from security side, we need to track any config change for audit; also KMS access logs for the period — Samir will push that later.
[03:10] Jordan: noted. sofia, on your end — pilot patch that reduces eviction aggressiveness?
[03:15] Sofia: i have a patch that reduces eviction pressure and adjusts prefetch window; needs a small runtime rebuild and smoke test. estimated 2–3 hours for nightly deploy, but we want to run perf bench first on a dedicated pool so we can measure delta.
[03:33] Leanne: what's the risk of rollback if that patch causes memory to spike?
[03:37] Sofia: good question — we'll include an autoscale-safe rollback: if memory exceeds threshold we revert to previous image and route to fallback model variant. fallback correctness should be validated.
[03:50] Carlos: can you explain fallback model variant? last time fallback responses were slower and increased front-end timeouts.
[03:57] Sofia: yes — fallback is a lower-capacity model we keep for availability. it trades off accuracy for speed and is intended for transient degraded conditions. we need better traffic shaping to reduce timeouts.
[04:14] Priya: timeline expectation — we asked for a remediation sprint; how soon can we start?
[04:20] Jordan: propose sprint start 2027-01-11, two weeks, focused on: bench + patch validation (week 1), gradual rollout + monitoring + runbook (week 2). Ethan will coordinate invites.
[04:34] Ethan: i'll send invites; also suggest a pre-sprint checkpoint 2027-01-04 to align owners.
[04:41] Samir: regarding compliance — we will need SOC 2 log extracts, KMS rotation proof and RBAC matrix for the time of incident. Jordan/Ethan, can you provide guidance on artifacts and where to pull them?
[04:55] Jordan: yes we'll share a checklist and sample reports; there is an internal doc — i'll attach a template to the RCA.
[05:05] Priya: excellent. on the bench side, what are the metrics we want to capture?
[05:09] Sofia: token throughput p50/p95, cold-warm cache miss rates, memory usage over time, prefetch hit ratio, and fallthrough counts. also latency distribution during scaled-up nodes vs warmed nodes.
[05:23] Carlos: we'll provide traces and flamegraphs for the eviction windows — can attach to confluence.
[05:29] Jordan: perfect. next, can we talk about the permanent mitigations — long-term: tune autoscaler to avoid churn, KV cache TTL rework, pre-warm hooks and staged routing, and maybe reserved dedicated capacity for peak windows.
[05:47] Leanne: dedicated capacity is interesting but we need cost estimate. We'll evaluate if reserved will buy stability.
[05:54] Jordan: Sofia can produce an estimate for dedicated pool TCO and expected p95 improvements as part of bench results.
[06:01] Sofia: yes i can; i'll include a few sizing options (small, medium, large) and expected latency tails.
[06:08] Priya: one more thing — the incident showed sequences where KV keys were mis-attributed across shards; is that likely a runtime bug?
[06:16] Sofia: we observed rare key-collision logs; possibly due to segmentation after restart. we need to reproduce in staging; that's part of the remediation backlog.
[06:28] Carlos: i'll try to reproduce with a mempressure test and share steps.
[06:33] Jordan: great. action items recap shortly. any questions from Tidewell security?
[06:39] Samir: just to confirm, will Redwood share a whitebox log set or will we be consuming via API? we need raw events for audit.
[06:45] Ethan: we'll provide redacted raw logs via secure Confluence link / S3 with ACLs. Samir, we'll coordinate access and retention length.
[06:55] Priya: today i want a short-term mitigation checklist — which we can run now: cap autoscale, raise kv buffer, route to warmed nodes, enable extra tracing. who owns each?
[07:06] Jordan: cap autoscale — Carlos (customer) action; raise kv buffer — Sofia (Redwood) will push patch; route changes — Jordan + Carlos to coordinate; extra tracing — Ethan will enable and hand over logs.
[07:20] Carlos: acknowledged.
[07:24] Leanne: how do we measure success for the sprint?
[07:27] Jordan: success criteria: p95 latency reduced to pre-incident baseline within 1.5x, <1% error rate during peak, reproducible bench showing reduced cold miss penalty, and a validated rollback plan.
[07:42] Priya: those look reasonable. please add SLOs to the sprint backlog.
[07:46] Jordan: will do.
[07:48] Sofia: one technical note — our runtime has a warmup hook that wasn't firing reliably under certain kube node churn patterns; investigating a fix to delay traffic after node join until warm hook completes. that'll be in the backlog.
[08:05] Carlos: that aligns with our observations.
[08:10] Jordan: ok next we discussed monitoring and alerts — need finer-grained KV miss alerting, combined with autoscale activity and warmup telemetry. Ethan will add dashboard widgets.
[08:21] Ethan: will do. I'll share a dashboard link in the RCA.
[08:25] Samir: about the SOC 2 artifacts — i'll need login events, KMS access logs and a short writeup of config changes. we'll accept redacted logs but need chain-of-custody.
[08:36] Jordan: understood — we'll provide that.
[08:40] Priya: any blockers on Redwood side for performing the bench?
[08:44] Sofia: need your approval for a short reserved capacity window and creds to your staging VPC for realistic perf. also need to confirm data privacy constraints.
[08:55] Priya: we can provide staging VPC limited creds — i'll send details.
[09:00] Jordan: excellent. last part — timeline and cadence: 2026-12-31 Carlos to upload traces; 2027-01-02 Jordan to send RCA draft; 2027-01-04 pre-sprint checkpoint; 2027-01-07 bench results; 2027-01-11 sprint start. sound good?
[09:20] Leanne: yes.
[09:22] Samir: yes — and i'll share audit items by 2027-01-06.
[09:28] Jordan: cool — thanks everyone. we'll capture action items in Confluence and follow up in the pre-sprint.
[09:35] Priya: thank you, appreciate the responsiveness.
[09:38] Jordan: thanks, happy holidays all.

Notes on transcription: occasional crosstalk, a few proper nouns mistranscribed (prefetch shown as prefetching, KV sometimes as K V). references: RCA draft link (Confluence): https://confluence.tidewell.example/RCA-2026-12-incident, bench spreadsheet: https://s3.redwood.example/tidewell/benchmarks/2026-12-27.xlsx

End of transcript.
questions: What is the immediate rollback plan if the eviction patch regresses memory?
Can Redwood produce a TCO estimate for dedicated pool options?
What exact SOC 2 artifacts will Tidewell need for the incident window?
